answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because lagoon only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, zephyr is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
